title: reservoir-admission-with-attention-kernel-hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We still see 99.9th percentile tail spikes on prefill+decode flows for heterogeneous traffic (short prompts mixed with long continuations). Current admission heuristics over-aggregate or over-shape batches, causing kernel mismatches and KV-cache churn which worsens tail latency.

Proposal: Implement a reservoir-based admission layer that temporally reserves a small ‘micro-reservoir’ for late-arriving high-affinity requests while shaping the main batch window aggressively. Admission decisions will consult an attention-hint estimator that tags requests with a kernel-preference score (optimal kernel / expected attention bandwidth / prefill length distribution). The admission layer will use these hints to influence window packing and to trigger targeted prefetches of KV slots and attention prewarm kernels before decode begins.

Goals: Reduce P99 end-to-end (client-observed) latency by 15-25% for mixed workloads, cut median decode kernel-switches by 30%, and reduce KV cache thrash for multi-tenant workloads. Maintain aggregate throughput within 5% of baseline and avoid regression on cost-per-token.

Scope: Runtime admission controller, lightweight attention-hint model, kernel-hint mapping table, prefill prefetch hook, telemetry dashboards, and a canary rollout path for dedicated clusters.

Non-goals: Full ML model retraining for attention hinting; this is an inference-time estimator with simple heuristics and a small tuned classifier. Not implementing cross-GPU global coordination in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Admission layer accepts and rejects requests using reservoir policy and exposes metrics for accepted/reserved/rejected counts
Attention-hint estimator annotates requests with kernel-preference and expected prefill length in request metadata
End-to-end P99 latency reduction >= 15% on internal mixed workload replay compared to current mainline
Kernel-switch rate during decode reduced by >= 25% on replay
KV cache miss-rate reduced on long-tail tenants by >= 20%
Feature gated behind runtime flag and disabled by default; toggles supported per-cluster and per-tenant
Automated end-to-end tests for correctness and unit tests for admission policy edge cases
Canary rollout plan documented with rollback criteria and monitoring playbooks
tasks: Design reservoir admission state machine and policy parameters
Prototype attention-hint estimator (lightweight classifier + heuristics) and benchmark inference cost
Implement kernel-hint mapping and local kernel selector hook
Integrate prefill prefetch API to warm KV slots and attention buffers
Add telemetry: acceptance rates, reservoir occupancy, kernel selection distribution, KV hit/miss, P50/P95/P99 latency
End-to-end replay test against mixed-workload trace and compare against baseline
Write feature gate and per-cluster config; implement canary rollout script
Document design, operational runbook, and performance benchmarks
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Created: initial design sketch and motivation. SLO target proposed: P99 -15%
2026-03-11 - Spike: built attention-hint prototype using token-length, prompt-entropy proxy, and model type. Inference cost ~0.02ms/request (native C++), acceptable
2026-03-12 - Implementation: reservoir admission state machine PR opened (diff: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4826). Local tests for fairness and starvation passed

2026-03-13 - Experiment: replayed 24h mixed trace on dev cluster. Observed 18% P99 improvement and 28% reduction in kernel-switch events in initial run. KV miss-rate improved ~14% (below target) which suggests additional prefetch tuning needed

2026-03-14 - Decision: Increase micro-reservoir size heuristically for multi-tenant workloads and add targeted prefetch of KV shards. Added tasks to tune mapping table for kernel hints. Preparing canary plan for two dedicated clusters next week
